predictions: P-A (BB union rule): the new fits will pass the union rule (LRT_BANDBB_BAND>=9.2 & BANDBB_KT>1.05  OR  LRT_CPLBB_CPL>=9.2 & CPLBB_KT>1.05) in the TIME-INTEGRATED spectrum and in AT MOST 3 resolved blocks. Archival: union in the integrated spectrum + exactly ONE of eight resolved blocks (blk4, 3.460-4.307 s), with integrated LRT_BANDBB_BAND = 9.85 (barely over the 9.2 threshold) and LRT_CPLBB_CPL = 22.18; blk4 gives 12.15 / 12.81. FALSIFIED IF the union count reaches >=5 resolved blocks, OR IF the integrated spectrum FAILS the union rule on both arms. *** THIS BURST IS PREDICTED TO BE A BB-POOR BURST, and for once there is an INDEPENDENT PHYSICAL-MODEL CHECK: Acuner+2020 (2020ApJ...893..128A) fitted the brightest bin (2.68-3.53 s, S=56.61) with slow-cooled synchrotron (SCS, electron index p=3.8) and a non-dissipative photosphere (NDP) and got ln Z_CPL = -913.47 > ln Z_SCS = -925.93 > ln Z_NDP = -966.25, i.e. the photosphere is disfavoured by Delta ln Z = 40.3 against synchrotron (their P = 0.98) and 52.8 against the empirical CPL, with AIC_NDP - AIC_SCS = 1938.67 - 1860.43 = +78.24. If our engine returns a STRONG blackbody in the block covering 2.68-3.53 s, that is a direct conflict with the only published physical-model comparison of this burst and must be reported as such, not smoothed over. ***

P-A2 (kT class - a DELIBERATELY sharp, easily-falsified prediction): where a BB is preferred at all, the fitted kT will be HIGH, not the L28 edge-constrained low-kT class. Archival Band+BB kT values are 7.2, 60.9, 27.7, 25.9, 17.9, 21.0, 12.5, 28.4 keV (integrated 21.5) and CPL+BB kT 26.0, 26.3, 27.7, 11.5, 17.9, 2.6, 12.7, 26.9 keV (integrated 22.2) - a median around 22 keV, more than 2.5x the 8.1 keV NaI low-energy edge, i.e. NOT pinned at the edge. FALSIFIED IF the median preferred-BB kT in the new run falls below 8 keV. NOTE THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE ALREADY IN HAND: the archival Band+BB kT errors are MISSING (null) in 6 of 9 rows and blk1 returns kT = 60.87 keV with no error at all, so several of these are unconverged/unbounded and the 'high-kT class' claim rests mainly on blk0 (7.20 +1.79/-1.88), blk4 (17.86 +4.01/-2.28) and blk6 (12.54 +4.97/-7.74). This prediction is therefore flagged WEAK in advance.

P-A3 (two-break): the new integrated LRT_DSBPL_SBPL will stay BELOW 9.2, and at most 2 resolved blocks will exceed it. Archival: integrated 2.76; of eight resolved blocks only blk4 exceeds 9.2 (11.30), the rest run 0.24-4.08. FALSIFIED IF the integrated LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2. ** A HARD VALIDITY CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS NUMBER: DSBPL_VALID is FALSE in every single archival row (9/9), so the archival DSBPL LRT values are being read off fits the engine itself declared invalid, and the archival break energies (xb, xp) show the classic swap pathology - xb > xp in the integrated fit (86.48 vs 51.84) and in blocks 1, 2 (95.05 vs 37.71; 111.31 vs 402.74 is ordered but blk1 is not), with xp railing near 400 keV in blocks 0 and 2. The correct reading of the archival prior is 'the two-break model never converged validly on this burst', NOT 'two breaks were tested and rejected'. If the hardened engine now returns VALID DSBPL fits, this prediction's baseline is void and the comparison must be re-derived. **

P-B (time-integrated Band frame, WITH the coverage correction stated in advance): the new time-integrated Band fit over the stamped -2.0 -> +14.0 s window with n0,n1,n2,n5,b0 will give Ep = 150-230 keV, alpha between -0.90 and -0.55, beta between -2.0 and -2.8, all well-constrained. FALSIFIED IF integrated Ep < 120 keV or > 300 keV, or if beta rails. Frames to diff against, each with its component coverage (T9): (i) GBM catalog flnc_band over -1.024 -> +28.672 s with b0,n1,n2,n5: Ep = 151.96 (+8.41/-9.21) keV, alpha = -0.8006 (+0.0440/-0.0461), beta = -2.0894 (+0.0549/-0.0472), Castor C-STAT red-chi2 1.1691/444 - TOTAL coverage (main pulse + the whole soft tail); (ii) GCN 13785 PRELIMINARY Band over +0.003 -> +10.496 s: Ep = 162 +/- 8 keV, alpha = -0.76 +/- 0.04, beta = -2.15 +/- 0.06 - MAIN pulse; (iii) Konus-Wind CPL over KW T0 -> +8.448 s = GBM -3.382 -> +5.066 s, 20 keV - 10 MeV: Ep = 225 (-19/+23) keV, alpha = -1.05 +/- 0.1 (90% CL), chi2 100.3/84 - MAIN pulse only, different band, different model; (iv) archival over -0.0995 -> +10.683 s: Ep = 185.56 (+10.10/-9.38), alpha = -0.827, beta = -2.560. *** COVERAGE PREDICTION, falsifiable: T90 = 21.248 s from T90START = +0.512 s so the burst runs to ~ +21.76 s and Konus sees emission to ~ +30 s, while our window closes at +14 s - we cover roughly 64 percent of T90 and omit the softest end of the tail. Our integrated alpha must therefore come out HARDER (less negative) than the catalog's -0.80, and our Ep HIGHER than the catalog's 152 keV. If instead we reproduce alpha = -0.80 and Ep = 152 keV on a 15-s-shorter window, suspect our background or response, not the catalog. *** SECONDARY CHECK: our window is close to the GCN's 0.003-10.496 s frame, whose Band gives Ep = 162, alpha = -0.76, beta = -2.15; the archival run on an almost identical span gave Ep = 185.6, alpha = -0.83, beta = -2.56, i.e. a ~15 percent Ep excess and a notably steeper beta. Reproducing that offset again would make it a real methodological difference worth chasing; not reproducing it would make the archival value the outlier.

P-B2 (evolution class = INTENSITY TRACKING - the sharpest and best-corroborated prediction on this burst): the block-resolved Band Ep will RISE from the first resolved block to a maximum in the block containing or immediately preceding the flux peak at t ~ 2.6-3.5 s, and only then decay monotonically. There will be NO pure hard-to-soft track. FALSIFIED IF the block-Ep maximum falls in the FIRST resolved block (pure h.t.s.) or if Ep is monotonically decreasing across the whole window. Corroboration, four independent analyses using three different pipelines: (a) Lu+2018 Table 4 classifies bn120919309 as 'T' = Tracking (their footnote: 'H: H2S spectral evolution pattern; T: Tracking spectral evolution pattern'); (b) Yu+2019 Table 1 class 'i.t.'; (c) Wang+2024 RAA Table 3 Ep-evolution 'i.t.'; (d) Li+2026 Class II (Ep peaks before the flux peak) with t_p(Ep) = 2.27 +/- 0.41 s vs t_p(F) = 3.43 +/- 0.76 s. The published Ep tracks all rise-then-fall: Lu+2018 Band 157.08 -> 187.91 -> 258.47 -> 250.12 -> 135.83 -> 103.28 -> 27.85 keV over -0.45 -> 10.56 s; Yu+2019 CPL 213.27 -> 375.54 -> 309.38 -> 202.74 -> 185.74 -> 111.20 -> 59.81 keV over 0.31 -> 9.30 s; and our own archival Band 163.17 -> 186.31 -> 277.78 -> 253.93 -> 188.97 -> 139.32 -> 103.29 -> 55.69 keV over -0.0995 -> 10.683 s, peaking in blk2 (2.082-2.656 s). The GBM catalog's own peak-flux interval is 3.072-4.096 s and Lu+2018's KRL peak time is t_m = 3.21 +/- 0.06 s. SUB-PREDICTION P-B2b: the Ep maximum will sit at or BEFORE the flux-peak block, never after (all four papers agree on the sign; they disagree only on the size of the offset - see the recorded inconsistency below).

P-B3 (the line of death, and a LIVE PUBLISHED CONTRADICTION we must not resolve silently): the new block-resolved Band alpha will exceed the slow-cooling synchrotron limit alpha = -2/3 in AT LEAST 3 of the resolved blocks, but will NOT exceed alpha = 0 anywhere. Archival Band alpha by block: -0.331, -0.605, -0.580, -0.556, -0.656, -0.568, -0.838, -1.190 -> SIX of eight are above -0.667, none is above 0, and the integrated value is -0.827. FALSIFIED IF at most one block exceeds -2/3, or if any well-constrained block returns alpha > 0. *** THE CONTRADICTION (T5/L26 - LOGGED, NOT RESOLVED): Wang+2024 RAA Table 3 records this burst's 'alpha > -2/3' column as 'not all', i.e. SOME bins are above the line; Li+2026 Table 1 records f_{-2/3} = 0.00 for the same burst, i.e. NONE are. These are incompatible statements about the same data. A plausible mechanism is model dependence - Wang fits Band, Li fits CPL, and CPL indices run softer when beta is steep, which is exactly the regime here (Yu+2019's per-bin Band beta runs -2.3 to -4.0) - but that is a HYPOTHESIS, not an adjudication. Our own Band-vs-CPL pair in the same blocks is the natural test and should be reported as a resolution ATTEMPT, flagged as such. Independent anchors at peak flux, both CPL-family and both below the line: Acuner+2020 alpha = -0.65 +/- 0.06 (bin 2.68-3.53 s) and Ryde+2019 alpha_max = -0.66 (+0.04/-0.04); our archival Band alpha in the corresponding blocks is -0.580 and -0.556, i.e. ~0.09 HARDER - a real, small, model-attributable offset to quantify rather than to explain away. ***

P-B4 (high-energy index and the last block): beta will degrade toward the end of the window and the final block will lose its high-energy constraint. Archival blk7 (6.708-10.683 s) already returns BAND_VALID = FALSE with beta railed at -4.999 and Ep = 55.69 keV; Lu+2018's last bin (7.26-10.56 s) reports alpha = -0.53 +/- 0.00, a ZERO error bar, i.e. a failed uncertainty; Yu+2019's bins after 9.30 s are unconstrained (Ec near the 5000 keV rail, negative derived Ep) and their significance drops to S = 6.6, 2.2, 4.3. PREDICT the same handover, now pushed 3.3 s further out by the wider stamped window. FALSIFIED IF the final block returns a well-constrained beta near -2.3 with a finite two-sided error. NOTE: the extra tail our window buys (10.68 -> 14.0 s) is precisely the part every published analysis found unfittable, so it will most likely ADD an unconstrained block rather than improve the integrated fit.

P-C (identity and data provenance - NOT a fit target, stated so the P3 diff cannot blame any of it): SIX GCN circulars exist (13785 GBM, 13786 IPN, 13787 Konus-Wind, 13790 Swift-XRT, 13791 Swift-UVOT, 13821 Swift-XRT follow-up), all unambiguously for GRB 120919A. NO redshift is reported anywhere, in any circular or paper (Li+2026's z column is blank) - so every distance-dependent quantity is CLOSED for this burst. NO afterglow: two uncatalogued XRT sources in the IPN box, NEITHER fading over 134-573 ks (GCN 13821 verbatim: 'implying we have not detected any X-ray counterpart to this GRB'), UVOT m2 > 21.4, GROND non-detection at 2.67 d (Greiner+2024 Table 5). NO LAT and NO LLE: theta = 62.1455 deg off the LAT boresight (tcat THETA), grb_sample HAS_LAT = False, and the FSSC current/ directory for this trigger contains no gll_* product at all - so the DataInventory D1 off-axis DRM check does not apply. Position adopted = the IPN box centre RA 214.768, Dec -45.564 (LOC_SRC = IPN, ERR_RAD = 0.4 deg), NOT the GBM ground position (213.4, -46.3, 1.2 deg away). Approved detectors n0, n1, n2, n5, b0 at 43.15, 22.74, 41.94, 35.11, 37.33 deg (recomputed from poshist this pass and matching the stamps to 2 decimals); n3 at 57.81 deg fails the 50-deg NaI rule. *** DETECTOR-SET NOTE FOR THE DIFF: the GBM catalog scat fits and BOTH published time-resolved analyses (Yu+2019, Wang+2024) use b0,n1,n2,n5 - four detectors. We approve those four PLUS n0 (43.2 deg). Our fits therefore carry one NaI that no published analysis of this burst used. That is a documented difference, not a defect, but any low-energy discrepancy should be tested against it (D5-style with/without diagnostic only - NEVER a production drop). ***

P-D (data-quality prediction, falsifiable at the background stage - and this is the one real hazard on this burst): the POST-BURST background window is contaminated by the ARR slew. GCN 13785 states verbatim 'this burst was bright enough to result in a Fermi spacecraft autonomous re-point request (ARR) maneuver', and the catalog row (Narayana Bhat+2016 p.82) carries the 'ARR' flag. VERIFIED LOCALLY IN THIS PASS from data/bn120919309/glg_poshist_all_120919_v01.fit: the source-to-spacecraft-+z angle drifts at the constant orbital rate +0.038 deg/s until t = +43 s, then reverses and sweeps 63.8 deg -> 12.0 deg between +45 s and +290 s. The stamped post-burst background window is +24.0 -> +115.0 s, so it STRADDLES the slew onset - roughly its first 19 s are on stable attitude and its last 72 s are mid-slew, by the end of which the geometry has moved ~11 deg. PREDICT: the post-burst polynomial segment will show a systematic level/curvature mismatch against the pre-burst segment (-33.0 -> -12.0 s, entirely on stable attitude), and the resulting background bias will fall hardest on the LATE blocks - i.e. on exactly the soft-tail blocks where P-B4 says the fit is already fragile. FALSIFIED IF the pre- and post-burst background levels agree within statistics and the post-burst residuals are flat. *** EXPLICITLY NOT SAA: the poshist SAA bit is set only during -3643 -> -2565 s and +2172 -> +3632 s, so the nearest SAA exit is 2565 s (43 min) before the trigger and the nearest entry 2172 s after - this burst is NOT a bn110920546-style activation-tail case. The flag that IS set at trigger (FLAGS = 1) is the ~51%-duty orbital sunlight bit, not SAA. *** SEPARATE CHECK PERFORMED AND CLEAN: results/human_review_qc_flags.txt carries no entry for this trigger, so there is no accepted source-overruns-background-gap decision to respect here.
